what_happened: Research confirmed the full gate-lock mechanism can be built from existing task-lock.sh primitives (acquire_named_mutex, commit-acquire/release pattern, resolve_session_pid, session_liveness) with zero new concurrency primitives -- only two new CLI subcommands and two call-site wirings.

The research report settled the lease-vs-advisory question with a concrete reuse surface (acquire_named_mutex plus a commit-acquire-shaped CLI pair) and exact call sites, so planning needed no re-derivation of the design -- only grounding reads to confirm it. Planning time went to integration detail rather than design.

Four integration constraints were found by plan-time source reads that the research report did not surface, each of which would have produced a broken or self-defeating implementation if planned from the report alone: the source-store task-lock.sh copy exits 1 under deploy-root-guard.sh so both call sites must invoke the deployed copy; run-all.sh already installs a per-branch EXIT trap on each of its two execution paths, which would silently clobber a top-level gate-lock release trap and leak the mutex for a full staleness window; a --only-narrowed run must skip the lock or suite narrowing (the sanctioned sub-full tier discharge mechanism) would be taxed with a full-battery wait; and the new fixture suite must clear inherited RUN_ALL_NESTED/GATE_MUTEX_HELD or its unnested cases go vacuous when run under an outer battery. All four are now recorded in the plan's Research Integration section.

First draft of verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run() gate-lock bracket checked VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED directly, but that variable is unconditionally exported near the top of verify-deploy.sh (its own self-nesting guard) long before gate8_run() runs, so the check always read 1 and gate8_run()'s own acquire was always skipped -- confirmed live via a real --only-gate 8 run showing run-all.sh itself (not verify-deploy.sh) as the mutex owner. Fixed by capturing VERIFY_DEPLOY_WAS_NESTED_AT_ENTRY before the unconditional export, mirroring tests/run-all.sh's own RUN_ALL_WAS_NESTED_AT_ENTRY pattern.

Phase 5's contended before/after measurement captured the fail-open safety property live against the real repository: with GATE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS=0, one of two concurrent --only-gate 8 invocations exhausted its wait budget and fail-opened with a named WARNING naming the holder, then ran its own real battery anyway, genuinely overlapping with the winner (load peaked 16.75). The generous-budget window showed true serialization (no overlap, load stayed 2.4-5.5) with live progress-reporting lines naming the holder every 15s. An initial mislabeling of the budget=0 window as a 'lock-disabled baseline' was caught during review and corrected in the plan body: it is fail-open evidence for an active bracket, not the non-vacuousness baseline (which Phase 4's fixture already establishes by removing the deployed task-lock.sh entirely).
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 2's git-commit-phase.sh call silently dropped agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-run-all-parallel.sh from the phase commit because that path was not in task 413's declared file_scope (the Containment Self-Check's drop-and-warn fail-safe, working exactly as designed) -- but the WARNING line was not scrutinized at the time, so the file sat as an uncommitted deviation fix across Phases 2-6 undetected until a routine pre-Phase-7 git-status re-check caught it. Fixed by committing it directly via git-commit-scoped.sh in Phase 7. The same thing happened independently for agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json in Phase 6 (a line_count-index fix this task's own prose edits required), caught immediately that time because the phase-closing commit's own stdout was read. Lesson for future dispatches: when a file touched mid-phase is not in the task's own declared file_scope, either add it via the sanctioned research/plan-stage --file-scope-add mechanism before implementing, or explicitly verify the phase-closing commit's WARNING output names every expected file -- do not assume git-commit-phase.sh's summary line alone confirms full containment.

Phase 7's full gate-set run's sole NEW failure (beyond the dispatch's enumerated known-unrelated set) was test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, traced to an uncommitted foreign working-tree mutation in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (lines ~2170/2183, 'while IFS= read -r f; do' changed to 'while false && IFS= read -r f; do') -- that suite's own documented deliberate-break regression-anchor technique, left un-reverted by whichever other task exercised it. Not in this task's declared file_scope, most recent commits on that file belong to other tasks, and a 'while false &&' guard is never legitimate production code. Not fixed by this task; left for the file's owning task/session to revert.
